title: Azure Container Registry, Container Instances and Container Apps
learningObjective: Create and secure a container registry, build and push images, and run containers on ACI and Container Apps with the right sign-in, networking, restart and revision settings.
foundation: A container packages an application with everything it needs, so it runs the same everywhere. Images are stored in a registry, and Azure Container Registry (ACR) is Azure's private registry.
Azure Container Instances (ACI) runs a container quickly with no servers to manage. It suits simple tasks and short-lived jobs.
Azure Container Apps runs containerised apps and microservices with HTTPS ingress, automatic scaling (even to zero), and versioned revisions.
engineer: Azure Container Registry (ACR) names: 5 to 50 letters and numbers, unique across Azure (<name>.azurecr.io).
ACR tiers (SKUs): Basic, Standard and Premium differ in storage and speed. Only Premium has geo-replication, private endpoints, content trust and dedicated agent pools.
Building images: in the cloud with az acr build (ACR Tasks, no Docker needed on your machine), or locally with docker push after az acr login.

Signing in to ACR: Entra identities with the AcrPull or AcrPush role (managed identities for Azure services, service principals for CI pipelines); repository-scoped tokens; the admin user, which is off by default, is one shared password, and isn't recommended. Anonymous pull is an option on Standard and Premium.
Azure Container Instances (ACI), the container group: the unit you deploy. Its containers run on the same host and share network, lifecycle and volumes. Groups with several containers are Linux only.

ACI settings: CPU and memory per container; OS type; ports; a public IP with an optional DNS name (<label>.<region>.azurecontainer.io), or a private IP in a VNet subnet; environment variables, with secure values for secrets; Azure Files volumes.

ACI restart policy: Always, the default, restarts the container every time it stops; OnFailure restarts only if it fails; Never doesn't restart. For jobs that should finish and stop, use OnFailure or Never.
ACI and a private registry: it needs registry credentials or a managed identity with AcrPull.
Container Apps, the environment: apps run in a Container Apps environment, which shares a VNet and logging.
Container Apps ingress: external (internet) or internal (VNet only), with a target port, and HTTPS automatically.

Container Apps revisions: a revision is a saved, unchangeable version of the app. Changing the image, containers or scale rules creates a new one. Single revision mode replaces the old revision. Multiple revision mode lets you split traffic between revisions (blue/green, canary).
Container Apps extras: secrets; managed identities; Dapr; jobs.

Which one to pick: ACI for a simple single container or a batch job; Container Apps for web APIs, microservices and event-driven apps that need scaling and revisions; AKS when you need full control of Kubernetes.

example.title: A nightly job and a public API
body: A nightly clean-up container runs on ACI with restart policy OnFailure. It stops when it's done, so you only pay while it runs. It pulls its image from ACR using a user-assigned managed identity that has AcrPull.
The public API runs on Container Apps with external ingress. Version 2 is deployed as a new revision and gets 20% of the traffic. After checking it works, the team moves traffic to 100%.

prerequisites: A resource group, and a Dockerfile or an image
For VNet deployment: a delegated subnet (ACI) or an environment VNet (Container Apps)
permissions: Contributor, to create registries and apps
AcrPush for CI pipelines, AcrPull for apps that run images
User Access Administrator or Owner, to give AcrPull
limits: ACR name: 5 to 50 letters and numbers
ACI resources are fixed per container group (redeploy to change them)
portal: Container registries > Create: name, SKU; Access keys (admin user); Networking (Premium private endpoints); Replications (Premium).
Container instances > Create: image source (ACR/Docker Hub/other), size, networking (DNS label, ports or VNet), Advanced (restart policy, env vars).
Container Apps > Create: environment, container image and resources, ingress, scale; Revisions blade: revision mode and traffic.
configuration.cli:
az acr create -g rg-app -n acrcontoso01 --sku Standard
az acr build --registry acrcontoso01 --image web:v1 .
az acr replication create -r acrcontoso01 -l northeurope   # Premium only
az role assignment create --assignee <principal-id> --role AcrPull --scope $(az acr show -n acrcontoso01 --query id -o tsv)
az container create -g rg-app -n aci-cleanup --image acrcontoso01.azurecr.io/cleanup:v1 --os-type Linux --cpu 1 --memory 1.5 \
  --restart-policy OnFailure --assign-identity <identity-id> --acr-identity <identity-id>
az containerapp env create -g rg-app -n cae-prod -l westeurope
az containerapp create -g rg-app -n api --environment cae-prod --image acrcontoso01.azurecr.io/api:v2 \
  --target-port 8080 --ingress external --registry-server acrcontoso01.azurecr.io --registry-identity system
az containerapp revision set-mode -g rg-app -n api --mode multiple
az containerapp ingress traffic set -g rg-app -n api --revision-weight api--v1=80 api--v2=20
configuration.powershell:
New-AzContainerRegistry -ResourceGroupName rg-app -Name acrcontoso01 -Sku Standard -Location westeurope
$c = New-AzContainerInstanceObject -Name cleanup -Image acrcontoso01.azurecr.io/cleanup:v1 -RequestCpu 1 -RequestMemoryInGb 1.5
New-AzContainerGroup -ResourceGroupName rg-app -Name aci-cleanup -Location westeurope -Container $c -OsType Linux -RestartPolicy OnFailure

troubleshooting.symptom: ACI is stuck pulling the image: unauthorized.
troubleshooting.cause: No credentials or identity for the private registry.
troubleshooting.fix: Give the managed identity AcrPull and pass --acr-identity, or give registry credentials.

troubleshooting.symptom: An ACI batch job keeps running again and again.
A container app can't be reached from the internet.
troubleshooting.cause: Ingress is internal or off, or the target port is wrong.
troubleshooting.fix: Turn on external ingress with the port the container listens on.

troubleshooting.symptom: A new revision gets no traffic.
troubleshooting.cause: Multiple revision mode, with traffic fixed on the old revision.
troubleshooting.fix: Change the traffic weights, or send traffic to the latest revision.

comparisons.difference: Full Kubernetes: you manage node pools and the cluster. Container Apps hides Kubernetes from you.

comparisons.service: AWS ECR / ECS on Fargate / App Runner
comparisons.difference: ECR is like ACR. Fargate tasks are like ACI. App Runner and ECS services are like Container Apps.

misconceptions.reality: No. ACI has no autoscale. Use Container Apps or AKS.

misconceptions.myth: The ACR admin user is the recommended way to pull images.
misconceptions.reality: No. Use Entra identities with AcrPull.

misconceptions.myth: Every change to a container app creates a new revision.
misconceptions.reality: No. Only revision-scope changes do (image, containers, scale rules).

architectureDecisions: Build in the cloud with ACR Tasks: build agents don't need Docker installed.
Pull with managed identities: keep the admin user off.
Several regions: use Premium ACR with geo-replication.

learn: Azure Container Registry SKUs and access

steps.label: It works on my PC
steps.title: The app runs on the developer's laptop only
body: A container packages the app with everything it needs, so it runs the same everywhere.

steps.label: Registry
steps.title: Azure Container Registry stores your images
body: ACR is a private registry. SKUs: Basic, Standard and Premium (Premium adds geo-replication and private endpoints). Push images with docker push or build them in Azure with az acr build; copy public images with az acr import.
Pull with a managed identity that has the AcrPull role, rather than the admin user.

steps.label: ACI
steps.title: Azure Container Instances: just run it
body: ACI runs a container group (one or more containers) with the CPU and memory you choose, billed per second. Good for simple apps, jobs and tests. Restart policy: Always, OnFailure or Never. A public IP and DNS label are optional.

steps.label: Container Apps
steps.title: Azure Container Apps: run it like a service
body: Container Apps adds HTTP ingress, automatic scaling (including to zero), revisions for safe updates, and environments that share a network. Good for web APIs and microservices.

steps.label: Recap
steps.title: Containers
body: Build once, store in ACR, run on ACI or Container Apps.
recap: ACR: Basic, Standard, Premium (geo-replication, private link)
Pull with a managed identity + AcrPull
ACI: simple container groups, per-second billing

handsOn.title: Import an image into ACR and run it on Container Instances
handsOn.cost: Low. ACR Basic is about US$0.17 per day; a small container costs cents per hour. Delete the same day.
before: Signed in at portal.azure.com as Owner of a subscription (a free or pay-as-you-go account works). Work in a resource group called rg-az104-lab.
If rg-az104-lab does not exist yet: search 'Resource groups' > Create > name rg-az104-lab, region UAE North (or any region near you) > Review + create > Create.

steps.do: Search 'Container registries' > + Create. Group rg-az104-lab, registry name acr<yourinitials><number>, SKU Basic. Create.
steps.see: The registry Overview with a login server like acrxyz.azurecr.io.

steps.do: Cloud Shell: select the >_ icon at the top of the portal, choose Bash, and 'No storage account required' if asked.
In the portal open the registry > Services > Repositories.
steps.see: A repository named hello with tag v1.

steps.do: Open the registry > Settings > Access keys and turn on 'Admin user' (only for this lab).
steps.tip: In real projects use a managed identity with AcrPull instead of the admin user.

steps.do: Search 'Container instances' > + Create. Group rg-az104-lab, name aci-lab, image source: Azure Container Registry, registry: yours, image hello, tag v1, size 1 vCPU / 1.5 GiB.
Networking tab: DNS name label aci-lab-<yourinitials>, port 80 TCP. Review + create > Create.
steps.see: Deployment completes in a minute or two.

steps.do: Open aci-lab > Overview and browse to the FQDN.
steps.see: A 'Welcome to Azure Container Instances!' page.

check: The image is in your registry and the container serves a web page.
cleanup: When you finish for the day: Resource groups > rg-az104-lab > Delete resource group > type the name > Delete. This removes everything inside it.
